hook.situation: You check the weekend forecast before a trip, see typhoon and fine-dust warnings, and need to decide whether to bring an umbrella, cancel the schedule, or book again later.
objectives: Use 날씨, 일기예보, 비, 눈, 태풍, 미세먼지, and 우산 in forecast-based plan talk.
Connect weather words to real decisions with -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요, -(으)ㄹ 텐데, V면, N 때문에, and V(으)ㄹ 때.
Write a short message that delays, cancels, or rebooks a plan because of weather.
hook.whyItMatters: Weather words are not just description words. In daily Korean, they often explain why a plan changes: 비 때문에 못 가요, 미세먼지가 심하면 취소해요, 날씨가 맑아질 때 다시 예약해요.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 — a cautious forecast or guess
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when you are reading signs, a forecast, or the sky and want to sound careful rather than certain.
grammarNotes.formation: Add -ㄹ 것 같아요 after a vowel stem and -을 것 같아요 after a consonant stem. 오다 becomes 올 것 같아요, 맑다 becomes 맑을 것 같아요, and 늦다 becomes 늦을 것 같아요. In weather talk, this is the safest first sentence because forecasts can change.

examples.en: I think it will rain.
examples.note: A cautious forecast, not a promise.

examples.ko: 태풍이 올 것 같아서 비행기가 늦을 수도 있어요.
examples.romanization: taepungi ol geot gataseo bihaenggiga neujeul sudo isseoyo.
examples.en: It looks like a typhoon may come, so the plane might be late.
examples.note: The forecast explains why the plan may change.

examples.en: I think it will be cloudy tomorrow.
examples.note: Use the adjective stem 흐리- plus -ㄹ 것 같아요.

examples.en: I think the temperature will drop.
examples.note: A useful forecast sentence before giving advice.

exceptions: 비가 오는 것 같아요 means it seems to be raining now. 비가 올 것 같아요 means it looks like it will rain.

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㄹ 텐데 — likely situation plus concern
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when the forecast makes you worry, warn someone softly, or prepare the listener for a plan change.
grammarNotes.formation: Add -ㄹ 텐데 after a vowel stem and -을 텐데 after a consonant stem. In weather Korean, it often feels like 'it will probably be like this, so...' and the second half may be advice, concern, or a question.

examples.en: A typhoon will probably come; do you think the flight will be okay?
examples.note: The speaker is not just predicting; they are worried about the result.

examples.en: The fine dust will probably be bad; should we cancel the plan?
examples.note: A natural way to raise a concern before deciding.

examples.ko: 장마라서 비가 많이 올 텐데 우산 챙기세요.
examples.romanization: jangmaraseo biga mani ol tende usan chaenggiseyo.
examples.en: It is rainy season, so it will probably rain a lot. Bring an umbrella.
examples.note: Weather expectation leads to practical advice.

examples.en: It will probably drop below zero, so dress warmly.
examples.note: Useful for cold-weather warnings.

exceptions: -(으)ㄹ 텐데 is a guess or concern. Do not confuse it with -(으)ㄹ 건데, which often states the speaker's own plan.

grammarNotes.title: V/A면 — if the weather is like this
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this to set the weather condition first, then say what you will do.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -면 after vowel stems and -으면 after consonant stems. In this chapter it links weather to a decision: if it rains, bring an umbrella; if fine dust is bad, cancel the schedule.

examples.en: If it rains, take an umbrella.
examples.note: The condition comes before the action.

examples.ko: 미세먼지가 심하면 일정은 취소하는 게 좋겠어요.
examples.romanization: misemeonjiga simhamyeon iljeongeun chwisohaneun ge jotgesseoyo.
examples.en: If the fine dust is bad, it would be better to cancel the plan.
examples.note: A realistic plan-change sentence.

examples.en: If the weather is clear, let's book again.
examples.note: A simple rebooking condition.

examples.en: If the temperature drops below zero, the roads are slippery.
examples.note: A condition that explains a safety concern.

grammarNotes.title: N 때문에 — because of a weather cause
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when a noun such as 비, 눈, 태풍, or 미세먼지 is the reason a plan changes.
grammarNotes.formation: Put the noun directly before 때문에: 비 때문에, 태풍 때문에, 미세먼지 때문에. Do not add 가 or 를 before 때문에. This form often explains an unwanted result such as cancellation, delay, or inconvenience.

examples.en: I could not take a walk because of the rain.
examples.note: The noun 비 is the cause.

examples.en: The plane was late because of the typhoon.
examples.note: A common travel-disruption sentence.

examples.en: We canceled the plan because of fine dust.
examples.note: Directly connects air quality to a plan change.

examples.ko: 안개 때문에 앞이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.romanization: angae ttaemune api jal an boyeoyo.
examples.en: I cannot see well ahead because of the fog.
examples.note: Weather can also explain a safety problem.

exceptions: Use N 때문에 for nouns. For a full clause, use a clause form such as 비가 와서 or 미세먼지가 심해서.

grammarNotes.title: V(으)ㄹ 때 — when the weather happens
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this to name the time when the weather event happens, then say what action fits that time.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -ㄹ 때 after vowel stems and -을 때 after consonant stems. 오다 becomes 올 때, 맑아지다 becomes 맑아질 때, and 춥다 becomes 추울 때. This is different from V면: V면 sets a condition; V(으)ㄹ 때 points to the time or occasion.

examples.en: When it rains, I use an umbrella.
examples.note: The sentence focuses on the rainy moment.

examples.en: When it snows, the roads are slippery.
examples.note: Here 눈 means snow, not eye.

examples.en: When the fine dust is bad, I close the window.
examples.note: A daily-life air-quality sentence.

examples.en: Let's book again when the weather clears.
examples.note: The time marker supports the rebooking plan.

exampleSentence.en: Did you see the weekend forecast?
Let's book again when the weather clears.
I think it will be cloudy tomorrow.
When it snows, the roads are slippery.

exampleSentence.en: The temperature will probably drop below zero, so dress warmly.
I think the temperature will drop.

exampleSentence.en: I cannot see well ahead because of the fog.

lines.grammarNote: 일기예보를 보다 is the natural first action before changing plans.

lines.romanization: taepungi ol geot gataseo bihaenggiga neujeul sudo isseoyo.

readingText.title: 태풍이 올 것 같아서 일정을 바꿔요
readingText.body: 민서는 주말 일기예보를 봤어요. 태풍이 올 것 같아서 비행기가 늦을 수도 있었어요. 또 미세먼지가 심하면 밖에서 오래 있기 어려워요. 그래서 친구에게 '미세먼지가 심하면 일정은 취소하는 게 좋겠어요'라고 보냈어요. 친구는 날씨가 맑아질 때 다시 예약하자고 했어요. 이처럼 날씨 표현은 단순히 하늘을 설명하는 말이 아니라, 약속과 여행 계획을 바꾸는 말로 자주 쓰여요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo checked the weekend forecast. A typhoon might come, so the plane could be late. If fine dust is bad, it is hard to stay outside for long. Minseo texted that it would be better to cancel the plan if the fine dust was bad. The friend suggested booking again when the weather clears. Weather expressions often change appointments and travel plans.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 태풍이 오면 무엇이 늦을 수도 있어요?
언제 다시 예약하기로 했어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 날씨가 맑아질 때 다시 예약하기로 했어요.

culturalNote.title: Weather talk often means plan talk
culturalNote.body: In Korean daily conversation, weather is often the reason for a practical decision. People may mention 일기예보 before travel, 태풍 before flights, 미세먼지 before outdoor plans, and 장마 before bringing an umbrella. The natural Korean move is usually cause plus action: 비 때문에 못 가요, 미세먼지가 심하면 취소해요, 날씨가 맑아질 때 다시 예약해요.
culturalNote.tip: For weather words, learn the verb that normally goes with the noun: 비가 오다, 눈이 오다, 안개가 끼다, 미세먼지가 심하다, 기온이 떨어지다.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence gives a cautious weather forecast?
inlineExercises.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 makes a cautious guess, and 비 uses the subject particle 가.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses 눈 as weather?
inlineExercises.explanation: In this chapter, 눈 is snow. 눈이 오다 means 'it snows.'

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence names fine dust as the cause of canceling?
inlineExercises.explanation: Use noun plus 때문에 without adding 가 or 를.
V(으)ㄹ 때 marks the time when the weather clears.

bullets: Core use: weather words explain real plan changes.
비, 눈, and 태풍 commonly pair with 오다; 안개 pairs with 끼다; 미세먼지 and 황사 often pair with 심하다.
-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 gives a cautious forecast, while -(으)ㄹ 텐데 adds concern or a soft warning.
N 때문에 explains a weather cause, and V/A면 sets the condition for what to do next.
